newsitem.title: USA: Bacou says sees one-time acquisition charge.
newsitem.headline: Bacou says sees one-time acquisition charge.

text.p: Bacou USA Inc said Tuesday the purchase of Survivair will result in one-time charges relating to purchased research and development of about $1.2 million and inventory step-ups of about $850,000 in 1997.
The company said on an annual basis it expects intangible amortization of about $800,000 attributable to Survivair.

In an 8-K filing Bacou released internal financial statements of privately held Survivair showing net income for 1996 of $1.6 million on net sales of $30.3 million, compared with net income of $2.3 million on net sales of $31.7 million for 1995.
Excluding discontinued product lines, Survivair had net sales of $29.6 million in 1996 and $30.8 million in 1995.
"We are on target to close this acquisition in the

second quarter," Stepan noted. "It will significantly broaden our respirator business and advance our plans for diversification within the personal protection equipment industry. We expect the addition of Survivair to our group of companies will be accretive to our earnings in 1998."

Bacou's net income for the first quarter of 1997 was $4.1 million, or $0.24 per share on 17.3 million weighted average shares outstanding, compared with net income of $4.1 million, or $0.30 per share on 13.9 million weighted average shares outstanding, for the first quarter of 1996. The 25 percent increase in weighted average shares outstanding resulted from the company's initial public offering of 3.5 million shares in March 1996. If the increase had been in effect for the first quarter of 1996, the company's net income for the first quarter of 1996 would have been $0.27 per share on 17.3 million weighted average shares outstanding.
